title: MERIDIAN CORE — Member Services Platform v4.2.1

teller.description: Standard teller. May inquire, transfer, open shares and update member information; Place Account Hold is refused with a supervisor-override screen.

supervisor.description: Supervisor. Additionally authorised for restricted functions such as Place Account Hold.

transactionToken.note: MERIDIAN's transactional forms carry a hidden token that must accompany the submission. Driving the real UI submits it inherently — the browser posts the form the operator sees — so the token is never read, stored, or reconstructed; the compiler only ASSERTS one is present before a posting step, so a form served without it fails loudly instead of posting something the core will reject. Two observed caveats, both grounded in committed evidence rather than assumed: it is NOT on every form (sign-on and member search post without one, which is why the assertion is emitted only for steps whose recorded state actually showed the field), and it is per-SESSION rather than strictly per-transaction — the same value recurs across forms within one session and changes between sessions.

faultInjection.note: The app forces a runtime condition per-request via ?inject=<kind>. The harness arms it as a one-shot request rewrite so it can land on a chosen step — including a form POST, which is the only way to exercise a fault on a review→post transition.

recoveries.description: The operator session ended mid-flow (idle timeout, or an injected 440). Recover by restarting from the entrypoint, which re-authenticates and mints a token bound to the new session rather than re-posting one bound to a session that has ended.
A scheduled-maintenance interstitial was served instead of the requested screen. It is transient: retry the flow from the entrypoint.
The signed-on operator is not authorised for this restricted function. Only a person can clear it: a supervisor must authorise the action on the live session.

handler.suggestion: This restricted function requires supervisor authority. On the live session, sign on as a supervisor and complete the action, then resume — the step's own postcondition will verify the result. If no supervisor is available, abort.

anomalies.description: MERIDIAN returned a hard application error (HTTP 500). Nothing on this screen can be trusted, so fail fast with the observed state rather than waiting out the step's clock.

outcomes.description: MERIDIAN could not locate the requested member record on this host. A legitimate answer for the caller to handle, not a failure of the automation.

MERIDIAN rejected the transaction as entered — a validation failure on the submitted values (an overdraw, a malformed e-mail or phone number). The caller should correct the inputs and retry. TWO markers, because the app renders this state on two different screens: the injected 400 shows a 'TRANSACTION REJECTED' banner, while a natural validation failure — an overdraw is the one the brief names — redisplays the form with 'The transaction could not be validated:' and a reason. Matching only the first reported every real overdraw as a hard timeout.

of.pattern: The transaction could not be validated
